why: All three checks pass, so the finding survives. (1) Doc quote is VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting.md, line 39 reads in full: "If memory usage stays high after these steps, run `/heapdump` to write a JavaScript heap snapshot and a memory breakdown to `~/Desktop`. On Linux without a Desktop folder, the files are written to your home directory." The second sentence of that two-sentence line does not reverse the claim - it is exactly the Linux fallback the claimed behaviour states. The following line (:41) supplies the rest of the claimed behaviour: "The breakdown shows resident set size, JS heap, array buffers, and unaccounted native memory ... the breakdown is the file ending in `-diagnostics.json`", plus a Warning block telling users to attach only the `-diagnostics.json` when reporting a memory issue. So `-diagnostics.json` is documented, not invented by the finding. (2) Absence confirmed with `grep -rai` (NUL-safe) across the whole repo excluding node_modules/.git/.references/.codegraph: the only hits for heapdump|heapsnapshot are this sweep's own artifacts (docs/superpowers/specs/data/*.json, the divergences .md/.tsv) and four vendored third-party Codex binaries under apps/electron/resources/bin/codex/. Zero hits in packages/, apps/*/src, scripts/. A wider search for the mechanism rather than the name - heapSnapshot, writeHeapSnapshot, node:v8, v8.getHeapStatistics, inspector - returns nothing in production source either, so the absence is of the capability, not just of the command name. (3) One layer up and one layer down, and the sibling-subsystem check: the near-miss surface is `process.memoryUsage()` in packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/server.ts:58 (server:getStatus returns memory {heapUsed, heapTotal, rss}) and :124 (getHealthCheck's 1.5 GB heap check, reused by the RPC handler, the headless HTTP health endpoint at webui/http-server.ts:212 and packages/server/src/index.ts:292). That is a different thing from what the doc specifies - three counters over RPC versus a .heapsnapshot file plus a four-way breakdown written to disk - and it is not user-reachable: the renderer's ServerSettingsPage.tsx consumes the unrelated settings:getServerStatus (running/host/port/tls/token shape in shared/config/server-config.ts), which carries no memory field, and `nessy-general-agent --help` lists no status command. The sibling diagnostic surface that DOES exist, apps/cli/src/doctor.ts, is deliberately scoped read-only to configuration (its docblock cites debug-your-config.md:46 and settings.md:208) and reports nothing about memory. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/foldSessionSummary) touches memory diagnostics. Not a deliberate product difference either: heapdump is not a subscription flow, not a gateway concern and not a rebrand, and unlike the same page's 200-row table cap and /terminal-setup it is not a terminal-renderer concern - a heap snapshot applies to any Node/Electron process, and this fork runs a long-lived Electron main plus a Pi subprocess, which is if anything a stronger case for it. The coverage map already scores the page consistently: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:175 marks `troubleshooting` red, traces but no implementation.
correctedState: No heapdump surface and no heap-snapshot capability anywhere in the fork: `grep -rai heapdump|heapsnapshot` over the repo hits only this sweep's own artifacts and vendored Codex binaries, and no production file imports node:v8/inspector or calls writeHeapSnapshot. The nearest thing that exists is process-level counters, not a dump: packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/server.ts:58 returns memory {heapUsed, heapTotal, rss} on the server:getStatus RPC, and :124 adds a pass/fail heap check at 1.5 GB reused by server:getHealth and the headless HTTP health endpoint. Neither is user-reachable - the desktop Settings page reads the unrelated settings:getServerStatus (no memory field) and the CLI exposes only `doctor`, which is read-only configuration diagnostics with no memory reporting. So the documented recovery step (write a .heapsnapshot plus a -diagnostics.json breakdown of RSS, JS heap, array buffers and unaccounted native memory to ~/Desktop, and attach only the -diagnostics.json when reporting) has no equivalent: a leaking Electron main or Pi subprocess still yields no shareable artifact.
